points.description: States that passing arguments by reference avoids copying (duplicating) the data — especially large data structures — when a function is called. Accept equivalent wording such as 'no copy is made', 'the function works on the original data instead of a copy', or 'saves memory/time by not duplicating large objects'.
points.partial_credit: Part marks for a vague efficiency claim without the no-copy idea, or for describing the mechanism only.

levels.says: Says passing by reference is more efficient, faster, or saves memory/time, but does not state that copying or duplicating the data is avoided.
Only describes the mechanism (the function receives the original variable/address, or changes affect the original), with no mention of avoiding copies or of efficiency.

rubric.notes: Full marks require the central idea that pass-by-reference avoids copying or duplicating the data (particularly large data structures) when a function is called, in any wording. Part marks are given for a vague efficiency or memory-saving claim that does not mention avoiding copies, or for a mechanism-only answer. Unrelated advantages, such as allowing a function to return multiple values, earn no marks unless tied to avoiding copies.
